title: Hyperlane network: continuous lanes and every connection
description: The lane network is drawn as one continuous picture across tile edges (lanes bridge the gap between hexes, merge at junctions, dock on systems) and shows one shortest route for every pair of systems that a chain of lanes joins. Before shots come from commit 95f9f878 (the earlier DY look), after shots from this branch; same capture scripts. Routes are computed once per layout (memoised, plus a generated table for the catalogue layouts).

shots.heading: Before: close-up of the five-tile chain, Race for Mecatol (desktop)
shots.caption: Each lane tile is its own fragment: the lanes stop at the tile edge and a ring cap sits in the 29 px gap between hexes, so a chain reads as separate pieces.

shots.heading: After: close-up of the five-tile chain, Race for Mecatol (desktop)
shots.caption: One continuous network: lanes run across the gap into the next lane tile, merge at junctions (diamond) and end in a dock ring on the system they reach. The dashed gold core marks the one chosen route per pair of systems.

shots.heading: Before: close-up of a junction, 3 players Hyperlanes
shots.caption: Lane ends of neighbouring tiles do not touch; where three lanes meet there is no junction mark.

shots.heading: After: close-up of a junction, 3 players Hyperlanes
shots.caption: Lanes flow through the shared edge; a diamond marks where three or more lanes meet; every lane end meets a system (dock ring) or another lane.

notes.title: Route choice
notes.text: Per pair of systems exactly one route: fewest lane segments, then fewest tiles, then the one sharing most already chosen segments, then lexicographic order of segment keys. Order of input does not matter.

notes.title: Engine
notes.text: The engine does not model hyperlane paths (galaxy.rs), so there is no engine adjacency to compare to; the tests check against plain graph reachability on every community map instead.

notes.title: Seams were the gap
notes.text: Hexes are drawn 150 apart with radius 70, so neighbouring edges are 29 px apart; the old per-tile art stopped at each edge. Lanes now run half the gap from each side (all the way to a system).
